source_refs.note: Exercise 8.4, Question 2 (book p. 253); answer key p. 307 (PDF 309).

blocks.prompt: 2. The flow rate of blood in an artery is modeled by the nonlinear equation \(Q = k\left(P - \frac{Q^{2}}{R}\right)\), where \(Q\) is the flow rate (mL/s), \(P = 100\) mmHg is the blood pressure, \(k = 0.05\), and \(R = 10\). Determine the possible real values of the flow rate \(Q\) accurate to two decimal places.
blocks.explanation:
Substituting the constants turns the model into a quadratic equation in Q, which has two real roots.
No method is named, so we use Newton-Raphson (fast, f' is easy) and check with the quadratic formula.
Plan: form f(Q) = 0, locate each root by a sign change, iterate, then decide which root is a possible flow rate.
steps:
Given: \(Q = k(P - Q^{2}/R)\), \(P = 100\), \(k = 0.05\), \(R = 10\).
To find: the real values of \(Q\) to two decimal places.
Method: Newton-Raphson \(Q_{n+1} = Q_n - f(Q_n)/f'(Q_n)\), because \(f\) will be a simple polynomial.

Form the equation
\[Q = 0.05\left(100 - \dfrac{Q^{2}}{10}\right)\]
\[Q = 5 - 0.005Q^{2}\]
\[f(Q) = 0.005Q^{2} + Q - 5 = 0\]
\[f'(Q) = 0.01Q + 1\]
Why: Newton-Raphson needs the equation in the form f(Q) = 0; f is a polynomial, so it is continuous and differentiable.

Iteration 1
\[Q_1 = 5 - \dfrac{0.125}{1.05}\]
\[= 5 - 0.1190 = 4.8810\]
Why: substitute Q_0 = 5 in the Newton-Raphson formula.

Which values are possible?
\(Q \approx -204.88\) would mean blood flowing backwards against the pressure, which has no meaning here, so it is rejected.
Why: a model can give mathematical roots that do not fit the real situation.

Check
\[Q^{2} + 200Q - 1000 = 0\]
\[Q = -100 \pm \sqrt{11000}\]
\[= -100 \pm 104.8809\]
So \(Q = 4.8809\) or \(Q = -204.8809\). Sign test: \(f(4.875) = -0.0062 < 0\), \(f(4.885) = 0.0043 > 0\), so 4.88 is correct to two places.
Why: the quadratic formula gives the exact roots and confirms both iterations.
blocks.final_answer: The real values are \(Q \approx 4.88\) and \(Q \approx -204.88\); only \(Q \approx 4.88\) mL/s is a possible flow rate.
